planting.note: Divide or repot rhizome clumps in spring as new growth begins; each division must include at least one healthy rhizome segment with roots to establish reliably.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light rather than the deep shade tolerated by the plain green species, since the cream and pale-yellow leaf sectors carry little chlorophyll and need stronger light to photosynthesize without stressing the plant. This chimeric sport of the standard ZZ plant produces new pinnate leaves that emerge streaked and blotched in ivory, cream, and pale yellow against the normal glossy dark green, with the proportion of variegation varying widely from leaf to leaf and even fading toward green as foliage matures. Because the variegation arises from an unstable genetic chimera rather than a fixed trait, propagate only from rhizome division rather than leaf cuttings to preserve the pattern, and prune out any shoots that revert fully to solid green before they dominate the clump. Allow the succulent rhizomes and potting mix to dry substantially between waterings, as for the standard species, since overwatering is the most common cause of rhizome rot in cultivation.
